column1: # mutation-provenance.tsv — WHICH CASES HAVE EVER BEEN KILLED, and by what.
# A mutation round establishes that the cases PRESENT AT THE TIME can fail. Cases
# added afterwards inherit that credential without earning it, and nothing in a
# suite's output distinguishes them: a case that survived ten mutants and a case
# that has never met one both print `PASS`. This ledger is what tells them apart.
# WRITTEN ONLY BY `monitor/mutation-gate.sh --record <this file>` — one row per
# case that FLIPPED in a subject-mutation round (and one row, against case `-`,
# for a round that flipped nothing). Never hand-edited: a hand-written kill is a
# claim, and this file exists because claims were all there was.
# which prints each CURRENT case as GUARDED (killed at the current suite and
# subject blobs), GUARDED-STALE (killed once; one of them has changed since) or
# NEVER-KILLED. Blobs are `git hash-object` of the working-tree file at the time
# of the round, so a row is checkable against any tree: `git cat-file -e <blob>`.
# `predict_blob` is the blob of the --predict file SNAPSHOTTED BEFORE EITHER ARM RAN
# (skeptic F1 on #1558); the 46 rows written before that column existed carry `-`
# and are unauditable on that axis — their `prediction` value is what the tool
# printed, not what a pre-registered file proves.
# APPEND-ONLY. A row is a measurement with a date; a newer round supersedes it by
# being newer, not by replacing it. `prediction` records whether the flip set the
# author wrote down BEFORE the run held — `refuted` rows are kept on purpose.
